notes: §1985:VI.6.21.4 GR2: "If an index-name is specified in the VARYING or AFTER phrase, and an identifier is specified in the associated FROM phrase, the data item referenced by the identifier must have a positive value." The rule binds the program and states no result for a value that is not positive, so the duty at 85 is that a positive value becomes the index's occurrence number. InitVaryingTarget initializes every VARYING and AFTER level whose variable is an index-name through SetEmitter.LandAmount and CobolIndex.TryAmount, which accept any integer the 64-bit index holds, and StoreSetTarget stores it. The only edition difference is 2023's EC-RANGE-PERFORM-VARYING raise, which BindVarying arms only when checking is enabled by a TURN directive, and 1985 has none; a zero value, which 1985 leaves undefined, sets occurrence 0 and the statement continues. The witness varies an index from an item holding 2. Probed further at --std 85: VARYING and AFTER indexes each initialized from an identifier (DISPLAY and COMP), with TEST BEFORE, TEST AFTER and an inline PERFORM, give the rule's elements.

next.reason: 1985: "the data item referenced by the identifier must have a positive value."; 2023: "If the data item does not have a positive value, the EC-RANGE-PERFORM-VARYING exception condition is set to exist.". Both require a positive FROM value when it initializes an index. 1985 states no result for a violation; 2023 defines one by raising EC-RANGE-PERFORM-VARYING.
